chapter_summary: Proverbs 28 confronts the reader with the sharp contrast between the righteous and the wicked across the whole of life — in personal character, in government, in money, and in relationships. It teaches that wickedness breeds fear and instability, while righteousness produces boldness, justice, and blessing. The chapter is particularly direct about the sins of oppression, greed, pride, and dishonest gain, and equally direct about the rewards of honesty, generosity, confession, and trust in God. Leadership is examined with unusual candour: a ruler without understanding crushes the people, while a leader who hates greed brings stability. The chapter reaches its peak in verse 13 — one of the Bible's most important verses on repentance: covering sin leads to ruin, but confessing and forsaking it brings mercy.
main_lesson: God blesses those who do right and confess when they do wrong. Wickedness always brings trouble, but walking in God's ways brings boldness, mercy, and blessing.

memory_verse.kjv: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.
memory_verse.little_bible: Hiding your sins does not work. But when you confess them and turn away, God shows mercy.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 28 is among the most theologically dense chapters in the book. It should not be read as a loose collection of moral tips but as a sustained argument: the wicked and the righteous are on entirely different trajectories, and the outcomes are not arbitrary — they flow from the character of God and the structure of His moral universe.

Verse 13 is the emotional and theological heart of the chapter and arguably one of the most important verses in all of Proverbs: 'He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.' This verse should be dwelt upon slowly with children. Hiding sin is instinctive — even young children do it. But Proverbs says the hiding strategy never works. The path to mercy is confession and forsaking: both are required. Not just admitting the wrong but turning from it. This is the Old Testament anticipation of the Gospel call to repentance.

The chapter also deals extensively with money and power. Verses on usury, oppression of the poor, greed, and dishonest gain (vv. 3, 8, 16, 20, 22, 27) form a repeated concern: wealth obtained wrongly does not last, and those who crush the poor will face God's justice. Verse 27 is one of Scripture's clearest promises: giving to the poor ensures you will not lack. This is a wonderful place to build generosity into children from a young age — not as an obligation but as a divine guarantee.

Finally, the chapter's treatment of leadership is worth extended family discussion. A ruler who lacks understanding becomes an oppressor (v. 16). When the wicked rise, people hide (v. 12, 28). But when righteousness leads, there is joy and increase. This is not just politics — it is a picture of any sphere of influence: parents, teachers, older siblings. Power used wisely brings life; power used selfishly destroys. Help your children begin to understand this early, and help them see their own growing spheres of influence as callings toward righteousness.
application_for_children: When you do something wrong, do not hide it. Tell God and tell the person you wronged. God promises to show mercy to those who confess and turn away from doing wrong. That is the brave and wise thing to do.

verses.kjv: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.
verses.little_bible: Wicked people run away even when nobody chases them. They are always afraid. But righteous people are as bold and brave as a lion.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Doing right makes you brave like a lion.
verses.meaning: Guilt produces a haunting fear — the wicked are always running, even from nothing. Righteousness, by contrast, produces a settled courage grounded not in personality but in a clear conscience before God. The lion imagery evokes strength, calm, and fearlessness — the natural state of the person walking in God's ways.
verses.prayer: God, help me live right so I am bold and not afraid.
verses.discussion_question: Why do wicked people feel scared even when no one is chasing them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that true courage flows from a clear conscience before God — and that fear and hiding are signals of a heart that needs to come back to righteousness?
verses.do_it_today: Think of something that makes you feel guilty or scared. Deal with it honestly today. Feel the boldness that comes from doing right.
verses.illustration_prompt: A shadowy frightened figure running from nothing on one side, and a confident child standing tall and calm like a lion on the other, bold warm watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged.
verses.little_bible: When a land is full of sin, leaders come and go quickly. But a wise leader who truly understands keeps things stable for a long time.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise leaders bring peace and stability to a land.
verses.meaning: Sin in a nation produces instability — a revolving door of competing leaders, none of whom can hold things together. But a leader of deep understanding creates conditions for long-term flourishing. This is a truth about the relationship between righteousness and lasting governance. A nation's health begins with the character of its leaders.
verses.prayer: God, give our leaders wisdom and understanding.
verses.discussion_question: Why does a wise leader help a country last longer and stay strong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children pray for and think about leadership — national, community, and household — as something God cares deeply about and that has real consequences?
verses.do_it_today: Pray for one leader today — a parent, teacher, pastor, or national leader. Ask God to give them wisdom.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two scenes: a kingdom in chaos with many arguing figures, and a calm wise ruler seated with people at peace around them, gentle watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: A poor man that oppresseth the poor is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.
verses.little_bible: A poor person who crushes other poor people is like a heavy rain that washes away all the crops. Nothing is left. Everyone suffers.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Hurting people who are already hurting is very cruel.
verses.meaning: The cruelty here is doubled: someone who has experienced poverty themselves, who should understand it, uses whatever small power they gain to oppress those even worse off. The image of a sweeping rain is vivid — it does not just fail to nourish, it actively destroys the food supply. Oppression among the poor is perhaps the most bitter form of injustice.
verses.prayer: God, help me never hurt people who are already hurting.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it especially cruel to hurt someone who is already suffering?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop empathy for those who are already vulnerable — and teach them that power over the weak is never to be used for harm?
verses.do_it_today: Look for someone who is already having a hard time today. Do one thing to help or encourage them.
verses.illustration_prompt: Heavy rain washing away a small field of crops, leaving bare empty ground, a poor figure watching helplessly, honest and sorrowful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: They that forsake the law praise the wicked: but such as keep the law contend with them.
verses.little_bible: People who disobey God's law end up praising those who do wrong. But people who keep God's law stand against wickedness.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Keeping God's law means you stand against what is wrong.
verses.meaning: How a person relates to God's law determines how they relate to wickedness. Those who abandon the law lose their moral compass and end up applauding what God condemns. Those who keep the law see clearly — and confront wrong rather than celebrating it. Our view of God's Word shapes everything else we see.
verses.prayer: God, help me love Your law and stand against all that is wrong.
verses.discussion_question: How does forgetting God's rules make you start thinking wrong things are okay?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children a deep love for God's Word — not as rule-keeping but as the lens through which they see clearly what is good and what is evil?
verses.do_it_today: Read one part of God's Word today. Let it show you something that is right and something that is wrong. Choose the right.
verses.illustration_prompt: One side: figures celebrating darkness and wrong; the other: a child standing firm with a bright open scroll, holding to God's law, warm courageous watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the LORD understand all things.
verses.little_bible: Wicked people do not understand what is right and what is wrong. But people who seek the LORD understand all things clearly.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Seeking God helps you understand everything.
verses.meaning: Moral and judicial discernment is not merely an intellectual capacity — it is a spiritual one. Evil, by its very nature, blinds a person to true judgment. Those who seek the LORD have their minds illuminated by Him, gaining the clarity to understand what is just, right, and good. This is one of the most important reasons to seek God: He gives understanding.
verses.prayer: God, help me seek You so I understand what is right.
verses.discussion_question: Why does seeking God help you understand more than not seeking Him?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children that wisdom and moral understanding are gifts from God received through seeking Him — not merely skills developed through experience or intelligence alone?
verses.do_it_today: Ask God this morning to give you understanding today — for one situation, one relationship, or one decision you are facing.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child seeking God in prayer, light and clarity flowing from above, while confused shadowy figures stumble in the dark nearby, warm and hopeful watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.
verses.little_bible: A poor person who walks honestly and rightly is better off than a rich person who lives the wrong way. Riches do not make someone good.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Being honest and poor is better than being rich and wrong.
verses.meaning: This verse is a direct challenge to the assumption that wealth equals blessing and poverty equals curse. God evaluates by moral integrity, not material wealth. The poor person of upright character stands in a more honourable place before God than the rich person living perversely — regardless of how each appears to the world.
verses.prayer: God, help me always choose right over wealth.
verses.discussion_question: Why is being honest and good more important than being rich?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a proper theology of wealth and poverty — rejecting both the prosperity gospel and the glorification of poverty, while holding integrity as the true measure of a person?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one situation where honesty might cost you something. Choose honesty anyway today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A humble child walking a straight bright path with nothing in hand, while a richly dressed but troubled figure walks a twisted dark path, warm watercolour moral contrast

verses.kjv: Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous men shameth his father.
verses.little_bible: A child who obeys God's law is a wise son. But a child who chooses wild and bad friends brings shame to their father.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Obey God's law. Choose wise friends.
verses.meaning: Wisdom is demonstrated both in personal obedience and in the company one keeps. A son who keeps the law honours his father. A son who runs with riotous, undisciplined companions brings public shame. The friends we choose are a direct reflection of — and influence on — our wisdom and our family's honour.
verses.prayer: God, help me obey You and choose wise friends.
verses.discussion_question: How do the friends you choose show what kind of person you are?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children evaluate friendships not just by fun or affection but by wisdom — asking whether this friend is drawing them toward or away from God and righteousness?
verses.do_it_today: Think about your closest friends. Are they wise? Do they help you follow God? Thank God for good friends, and pray for wisdom in choosing them.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child choosing to walk with a wise, good-hearted friend toward light, while a rowdy group goes the other way, clear and warm watercolour scene of a wise choice

verses.kjv: He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.
verses.little_bible: Someone who gets rich by cheating and charging unfair prices will only end up giving it all away to someone who will help the poor. Unjust money never stays.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Cheating to get rich never lasts.
verses.meaning: Usury here refers to exploitative lending that crushes the borrower. Money gathered through unjust means is under God's oversight — He redirects it. This is not merely karma; it is God's active governance of wealth. The ill-gotten gain of the oppressor will end up serving the very people the oppressor despised. God corrects the ledger.
verses.prayer: God, help me earn honestly and use money to help others.
verses.discussion_question: What happens to money that was gained by cheating or hurting others?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children that God sees every financial transaction — and that honesty in work, pay, and giving is a deeply spiritual matter, not just an ethical one?
verses.do_it_today: Think about how you got or use money. Is it honest? Ask God to help you handle money His way.
verses.illustration_prompt: Money flowing out of the hands of a greedy figure and landing gently in the hands of a person helping the poor, God's redirection visible in the scene, gentle watercolour

verses.kjv: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.
verses.little_bible: If someone refuses to listen to God's law, even their prayers are something God hates. You cannot ignore God's Word and then expect Him to hear you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Ignoring God's Word makes your prayers unwelcome to God.
verses.meaning: This is a sobering verse: the refusal to hear and obey God's law does not simply mean prayers go unanswered — it means they are an abomination. God is not a vending machine to be accessed for help while His Word is ignored. Obedience and prayer are inseparable. This does not mean sinners cannot pray for forgiveness, but it does mean wilful, ongoing rejection of God's Word corrupts the very act of prayer.
verses.prayer: God, help me listen to Your Word so my prayers please You.
verses.discussion_question: Why does God want us to listen to Him before we ask Him for things?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that prayer is relational, not transactional — and that listening to God and obeying His Word is what keeps the relationship with Him alive and real?
verses.do_it_today: Before you pray today, read one verse of Scripture. Let God speak to you before you speak to Him.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child covering their ears to God's Word while trying to pray, the prayer drifting away unheard, a contrasting panel showing a child listening first then praying openly, watercolour style

verses.kjv: Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good things in possession.
verses.little_bible: Anyone who leads a good person into doing wrong will fall into their own trap. But those who walk uprightly will receive good things.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Leading others into wrong traps yourself.
verses.meaning: The one who corrupts or misleads the righteous is not just harming another — they are digging their own grave. God's justice ensures the tempter falls into the very pit they laid for others. Meanwhile the upright receive an inheritance of good things. This verse vindicates those who are tempted and points the accusing finger squarely back at the one who tempts.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from leading anyone away from You.
verses.discussion_question: What happens to someone who tries to lead other people into doing wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand both the serious responsibility of their influence on others and the protection God provides for those who are righteous and being targeted?
verses.do_it_today: Think about your influence on others today. Are you leading anyone toward God or away from Him? Make it toward Him.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure digging a pit for others and then falling into it themselves, while a righteous upright figure receives good gifts from above, watercolour scene of justice and grace

verses.kjv: The rich man is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.
verses.little_bible: A rich man thinks he is very wise — but often he is just proud. A poor person with true understanding can see right through him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: True understanding sees through proud wealth.
verses.meaning: Wealth creates the illusion of wisdom — if things have gone well materially, a person often assumes they must be wise. But this is conceit, not wisdom. The poor person with genuine understanding from God can discern what the rich person's pride blinds him to. True wisdom is not wealth-dependent — it is God-given.
verses.prayer: God, give me true wisdom, not just pride in what I have.
verses.discussion_question: Why does being rich not automatically mean someone is wise?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children resist the cultural message that success and wealth equal wisdom — and instead build their understanding of wisdom as God-given discernment available to anyone who seeks Him?
verses.do_it_today: Think of someone you respect for their wisdom. Is it because of what they own or because of their character and knowledge of God?
verses.illustration_prompt: A proud wealthy figure surrounded by riches but confused, while a humble child with a glowing mind sees clearly and calmly, gentle watercolour contrast of wisdom and wealth

verses.kjv: When righteous men do rejoice, there is great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.
verses.little_bible: When righteous people are in charge and doing well, everyone celebrates and things are glorious. But when wicked people rise to power, people hide in fear.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Righteous leaders bring joy. Wicked ones bring fear.
verses.meaning: Leadership character determines the atmosphere of a community or nation. Righteous leaders create conditions where people can flourish openly and celebrate. Wicked leaders make people conceal themselves — out of fear, self-protection, and the instinct for survival. This is not merely political observation; it is a theological statement about how God designed human community to work.
verses.prayer: God, raise up righteous leaders in our land.
verses.discussion_question: How does it feel when good people lead, compared to when bad people lead?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand the deep connection between the moral character of leaders and the wellbeing of the people they lead — and to pray accordingly?
verses.do_it_today: Pray today for the leaders over your school, church, community, and country. Ask God to raise up righteous ones.
verses.illustration_prompt: Bright joyful people celebrating in an open square under righteous leadership, contrasted with hidden fearful figures huddled in shadow under wicked rule, powerful watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.
verses.little_bible: Hiding your sins will not help you. It will not make you prosper. But if you confess them and stop doing them, God will show you mercy.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Confess your sins and turn away. God shows mercy.
verses.meaning: This is the theological heart of Proverbs 28 and one of the most important verses in the entire book. Covering sin — hiding, excusing, minimising — does not lead to prosperity; it leads to ruin. But the person who does two things — confesses (brings the sin into the light) and forsakes (actually turns away from it) — finds mercy. Both parts are required. This is the Old Testament call to repentance, anticipating the full Gospel.
verses.prayer: God, help me confess my sins and turn away from them.
verses.discussion_question: What two things must you do to receive God's mercy when you do wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a family culture where confession is safe and celebrated — where children know that admitting wrong and turning from it is the brave and right path, not a path to shame?
verses.do_it_today: Is there something you have been hiding or making excuses for? Confess it to God today. Turn away from it. Receive His mercy.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child stepping out of shadow into warm light, holding a confession openly before God, gentle mercy flowing down, the contrast of hiding and confessing visible in a warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Happy is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.
verses.little_bible: The person who always respects and honours God is truly happy. But the person who makes their heart hard and refuses to listen will fall into serious trouble.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Honour God always. A hard heart leads to trouble.
verses.meaning: The 'fear' here is not terror but reverential awe — a constant awareness of and submission to God. This produces happiness, not anxiety. Its opposite is a hardened heart: the person who stops being sensitive to God's voice, who numbs themselves to conviction and correction. A hardened heart is always a prelude to a fall.
verses.prayer: God, help my heart stay soft and always honour You.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to have a hard heart? Why is that dangerous?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children stay soft and responsive to God — resisting the gradual hardening that comes through ignoring conscience, avoiding correction, or normalising sin?
verses.do_it_today: Ask yourself: is my heart soft toward God today? If something is making it hard, bring it to God and ask Him to soften it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A gentle child with an open soft heart full of light walking happily, beside a figure with a stony hard heart stumbling toward a hole in the ground, gentle watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.
verses.little_bible: A wicked ruler over poor people is as frightening as a roaring lion or a raging bear. He crushes the very people he should protect.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wicked rulers are dangerous like wild animals.
verses.meaning: The imagery is visceral and deliberate. A lion and a bear are apex predators — powerful, frightening, and deadly. A wicked ruler over the poor is exactly like this: dangerous, destructive, and a source of terror rather than safety. God does not soften this description. Leadership without righteousness is predatory.
verses.prayer: God, protect the poor from cruel and wicked rulers.
verses.discussion_question: How should a good ruler treat poor people? How does a wicked ruler treat them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a righteous indignation toward injustice — especially the oppression of the poor and weak — while also praying for God's justice to prevail?
verses.do_it_today: Pray for people around the world who are suffering under cruel leadership. Ask God to protect and rescue them.
verses.illustration_prompt: A roaring lion and a raging bear on either side of a frightened poor community, the shadow of a wicked ruler behind them, honest and sober watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The prince that wanteth understanding is also a great oppressor: but he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.
verses.little_bible: A ruler without wisdom and understanding becomes a great oppressor. But a ruler who hates greed will live long and lead well.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise rulers hate greed. That is what makes them last.
verses.meaning: The connection between a lack of understanding and oppression is stark: leaders who do not understand justice inevitably become unjust. But the antidote is specifically hatred of covetousness — greed, the desire to acquire more than is rightfully one's own. A leader who hates greed will not exploit those under their care. This person earns longevity because their leadership is life-giving rather than life-taking.
verses.prayer: God, help all leaders hate greed and love what is right.
verses.discussion_question: Why does hating greed help a ruler lead better and live longer?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate contentment and anti-greed in our children — helping them see that wanting what belongs to others is a root of injustice, not just a personal failing?
verses.do_it_today: Notice one moment today where you want something that is not yours. Stop. Choose contentment instead.
verses.illustration_prompt: A wise ruler seated calmly, turning away from a pile of gold with a firm look, people under their care living peacefully, long and stable reign visible, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.
verses.little_bible: A person who takes someone else's life will run toward their own destruction. No one should stop what is coming to them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Violence against life brings its own destruction.
verses.meaning: This verse speaks to the severity of bloodshed — the taking of a human life. The one who commits this violence will themselves rush toward the pit (destruction, death). The second clause — 'let no man stay him' — is a warning against interfering with God's justice. The consequence is certain, and attempting to prevent it is itself unwise.
verses.prayer: God, keep me and all I love far from violence.
verses.discussion_question: Why is hurting or killing someone always serious in God's eyes?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand the sanctity of human life — that every person is made in God's image, and that violence against life is an offence against God Himself?
verses.do_it_today: Thank God for the gift of human life today. Ask Him to help you protect and honour the lives of those around you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A troubled figure moving toward a dark pit under their own momentum, no one stopping them, God's justice at work in a solemn and honest watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once.
verses.little_bible: The person who walks honestly and rightly will be kept safe. But the person who lives in twisted and wrong ways will fall suddenly.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Walk right and be saved. Walk wrong and fall suddenly.
verses.meaning: Uprightness — moral integrity in one's way of life — comes with the promise of being saved. The word 'saved' here carries meaning beyond rescue from danger: it points to wholeness, preservation, and ultimate security. The perverse person, by contrast, does not decline gradually — they 'fall at once.' Their destruction is sudden. There is no warning-free descent into wrongness.
verses.prayer: God, help me walk in Your right way every day.
verses.discussion_question: What does walking uprightly look like in everyday life?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children build daily habits of integrity — understanding that the small honest choices accumulate into a life that is upheld and protected by God?
verses.do_it_today: Make one honest, upright choice today that you might otherwise have avoided. Walk right, just for today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child walking a straight bright path through open countryside, safe and secure, while a twisting dark path leads to a sudden drop elsewhere, warm hopeful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough.
verses.little_bible: The person who works hard on their land will have plenty of food. But the person who chases after worthless and lazy people will end up very poor.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Work hard and you will have plenty. Laziness brings poverty.
verses.meaning: Diligent work — represented by the farmer who tills the land — leads to abundance. Following 'vain persons' (empty, worthless, undisciplined companions) leads to poverty. The wisdom here is both practical and relational: what you work at, and who you follow, determine your outcome. The two dangers are idleness and bad company.
verses.prayer: God, help me work hard and not follow lazy or foolish people.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when you choose to follow lazy or foolish friends?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a work ethic in our children — not as a way of earning love, but as a reflection of God's own creative, diligent character — and help them see the connection between daily faithfulness and future flourishing?
verses.do_it_today: Pick one task you have been putting off. Do it fully today. See how it feels to work hard and finish well.
verses.illustration_prompt: A farmer contentedly tilling their field surrounded by growing crops, while a figure slumped against a wall with empty hands follows idle companions, warm watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.
verses.little_bible: A faithful person will be full of blessings. But someone who rushes to get rich quickly will not get away with what they do to get there.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Faithful people are blessed. Rushing to be rich leads to guilt.
verses.meaning: Faithfulness — steady, reliable, trustworthy obedience over time — produces abundance of blessing. The contrast is the person in a hurry to be rich: they will not be 'innocent' because the shortcuts taken to get there quickly always involve wrongdoing. Lasting blessing is built through faithful character, not financial shortcuts.
verses.memory_phrase: Be faithful. Not in a rush.
verses.prayer: God, help me be faithful and not greedy for quick riches.
verses.discussion_question: Why is someone who hurries to get rich likely to do something wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to build trust, faithfulness, and patience over time — pushing back against a culture that glorifies instant wealth and quick success?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one area where you are tempted to cut corners or rush. Choose the faithful, steady path today instead.
verses.illustration_prompt: A faithful person steadily walking a long blessed path covered in gifts and fruit, while a rushing figure stumbles and falls chasing a bag of gold, gentle watercolour wisdom scene

verses.kjv: To have respect of persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress.
verses.little_bible: Showing favouritism — treating some people as more important than others — is not good. Some people will do wrong for just a small reward. Do not be partial.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not show favouritism. Treat everyone fairly.
verses.meaning: Partiality in judgment — treating people differently based on who they are rather than what is right — is condemned here. The striking addition is the 'piece of bread': even the smallest incentive can lead a person who practises favouritism to transgress. Partiality corrupts justice at every level and for the smallest price.
verses.prayer: God, help me treat everyone fairly, not just my favourites.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to show favouritism? Why is that unfair and wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we build fairness into our family culture — treating each child, each person, and each situation with impartiality — and helping our children see favouritism for the injustice it is?
verses.do_it_today: Look for someone today who often gets left out or overlooked. Give them the same care and attention you give your favourite people.
verses.illustration_prompt: A judge or leader treating two different children with equal fairness, the scales of justice balanced, light and dignity for everyone in the scene, warm watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.
verses.little_bible: A person who rushes to get rich is greedy and cannot see clearly. They do not realise that poverty is heading straight toward them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Greed for quick riches brings poverty instead.
verses.meaning: An 'evil eye' in biblical culture means a greedy, covetous gaze — always looking for more, always calculating advantage. The person with this eye is so focused on getting rich quickly that they cannot see what is actually coming: poverty. Greed blinds. It makes the person ignore all the signs that their approach is self-destructive.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from greed and help me see clearly.
verses.discussion_question: How can wanting money too much make you end up with less?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a healthy, generous, content relationship with money and possessions — rather than the restless grasping that ultimately destroys what it seeks?
verses.do_it_today: Notice if you find yourself wanting something very badly today. Pause and pray about it. Ask God if your desire is wise.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure rushing toward a pile of gold, eyes wide with greed, not seeing the cliff edge just ahead, a gentle warning visible in a warm but honest watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue.
verses.little_bible: A person who honestly corrects someone will end up being more loved and trusted than a person who just says nice things to make them feel good.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Honest correction wins more trust than flattery.
verses.meaning: Flattery feels good in the moment but leaves people unchanged and uninformed. Honest correction is uncomfortable but it is a genuine gift — it gives a person a chance to grow, improve, and avoid harm. In the long run, the one who tells the truth gains more genuine favour and is more valued than the smooth flatterer.
verses.prayer: God, help me be honest rather than just saying nice things.
verses.discussion_question: Why is honest correction a kinder gift than flattery?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children both receive and give honest feedback — building the maturity to tell the truth kindly rather than hiding behind flattery to avoid discomfort?
verses.do_it_today: If you have been holding back honest feedback from someone to avoid an awkward moment, prayerfully consider whether you should share it kindly today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two figures: one whispering flattering empty words that dissolve like bubbles, the other speaking honest caring truth with warmth, the recipient growing wiser, watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer.
verses.little_bible: Someone who steals from their father or mother and says it is not doing wrong is as bad as a person who destroys everything. Stealing from your parents is very serious.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Stealing from parents is sin. Do not excuse it.
verses.meaning: Rationalising theft from parents — 'it is no transgression' — is the picture of a heart deeply hardened to conscience. The person who does this is called a companion of a destroyer: they are in league with the most destructive kind of character. The excuse-making makes it worse, not better. Calling sin by a comfortable name does not reduce its gravity.
verses.prayer: God, help me never steal and never excuse doing wrong.
verses.discussion_question: Why is making excuses for doing wrong just as serious as doing the wrong thing?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop the honesty to call sin what it is — not find softer words or justifications — and understand that God sees through every excuse?
verses.do_it_today: Think of something you have done wrong that you have been making excuses about. Stop excusing it. Call it what it is and confess it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child taking something from a parent and shrugging it off, a dark companionship forming in the shadows behind them, honest and sober watercolour moral scene

verses.kjv: He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the LORD shall be made fat.
verses.little_bible: A proud heart always starts trouble and fights. But the person who trusts in the LORD will be well fed and richly blessed.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Pride stirs up trouble. Trusting God brings blessing.
verses.meaning: 'Made fat' here is an ancient idiom for prospering abundantly — being well-fed, full, and flourishing. Pride stirs up strife because it always demands priority, resists correction, and refuses to yield. Trust in the LORD produces the opposite: a settled security that does not need to fight for position because God provides and protects.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust You and not be proud.
verses.discussion_question: Why does pride always start trouble with other people?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children distinguish between godly confidence and destructive pride — and cultivate the trust in God that makes pride unnecessary and strife avoidable?
verses.do_it_today: In any situation today where pride wants to start a fight, choose to trust God instead and step back. See what peace feels like.
verses.illustration_prompt: A proud figure surrounded by conflict and fighting, contrasted with a trusting child at rest, peace and abundance flowing to them from God, warm watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
verses.little_bible: A person who trusts only in their own feelings and ideas is a fool. But the person who walks in wisdom will be kept safe and delivered.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not trust only yourself. Walk wisely and be safe.
verses.meaning: Trusting one's own heart above all else — one's instincts, desires, feelings — is the definition of foolishness in Proverbs, because the heart is not a reliable moral guide on its own (see Jeremiah 17:9). Wisdom requires outside input: God's Word, wise counsel, correction. The person who submits to wisdom rather than self-trust walks toward deliverance.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust Your wisdom over my own heart.
verses.discussion_question: Why is trusting only your own heart and feelings dangerous?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children a healthy distrust of their own unchecked impulses — not making them fearful or insecure, but helping them learn to test their feelings against God's Word and wise counsel?
verses.do_it_today: Before making a big decision today, stop and ask: 'Is this what God's Word says? What would a wise person say?' Do not decide based only on how you feel.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child following only their own feelings into confusion, contrasted with a child checking God's Word and walking a clear safe path, gentle hopeful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.
verses.little_bible: The person who gives to those in need will never run out. But the person who looks away from the poor will face many curses.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Give to the poor. You will never lack.
verses.meaning: This is one of Scripture's clearest promises about generosity: give to the poor and you will not lack. God is the guarantor of this promise — He replenishes what is given in His name. The contrast is equally sharp: hiding your eyes from the poor (deliberately ignoring their need) brings not just failure to bless, but active curse. Generosity is not optional for the God-fearing person.
verses.prayer: God, make me generous to those who are in need.
verses.discussion_question: What does God promise to those who give to people who are poor?
verses.family_discussion: How do we make generosity a regular, joyful practice in our family — not occasional or reluctant, but a way of life grounded in God's promise that giving leads to not lacking?
verses.do_it_today: Find one way to give to someone in need today — time, food, money, or encouragement. Trust God's promise that you will not lack.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child generously giving to someone in need, and a gentle stream of provision flowing back to them from God, abundance and joy in the giving, warm bright watercolour scene

verses.kjv: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.
verses.little_bible: When wicked people rise to power, everyone hides in fear. But when wicked people are gone, righteous people grow and increase.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: When wickedness falls, righteousness grows.
verses.meaning: This verse closes the chapter with the same contrast with which it opened: the wicked and the righteous, and their opposite effects on the world. Wickedness in power suppresses and scatters. When the wicked perish, the righteous come out, multiply, and flourish. This is ultimately a statement of hope grounded in God's sovereign justice: wickedness does not endure, and righteousness has the final word.
verses.memory_phrase: Righteousness always has the last word.
verses.prayer: God, may righteousness always increase in our land.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think righteous people grow and increase when wickedness is removed?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children hold onto hope in times when wickedness seems powerful — grounding their confidence in the certainty that God's justice prevails and righteousness ultimately flourishes?
verses.do_it_today: Pray for one situation in the world where wickedness seems powerful. Ask God to bring it to an end and let righteousness increase.
verses.illustration_prompt: Dark shadows receding and falling away, with bright righteous figures emerging and multiplying in warm light, a scene of hope, increase, and God's justice prevailing, beautiful watercolour ending
